claims.claim: DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions must force untrusted project settings before reloading settings and resolving the bootstrap extension set.
The bootstrap pass now writes projectTrusted=false instead of true, so a previously-trusted state can no longer leak project extensions into trust resolution.
User/global and temporary CLI extensions still load during the bootstrap pass and are reused by the final extension set.
Regression coverage exercises the real loader through the read-only subject helper with settings/package/extension boundary fakes.

deliverables.change: Forced untrusted project settings in the trust bootstrap pass (setProjectTrusted(false) + reload before resolving extensions).
Standalone Node assertion regression for trust bootstrap isolation, final trusted/untrusted extension sets, and user/CLI extension availability.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node 24: exit 0 and 'regression: project extensions no longer leak into the trust bootstrap'. The script loads the real resource-loader.ts via .prale-eval/subject.mjs (createTrustSubject) with explicit settings/package/extension boundary fakes and asserts: (1) with initialTrusted=true the first trust write is [set, false] and the bootstrap resolve event observes loadedTrust=false; (2) the extensions handed to resolveProjectTrust are exactly cli.ts+user.ts, i.e. project.ts never appears in the bootstrap pass even though the prior state was trusted; (3) the bootstrap extension load event excludes project.ts; (4) after approval the final set is cli.ts+project.ts+user.ts with zero errors; (5) with initialTrusted=false and a rejected project, bootstrap and final sets are cli.ts+user.ts. Verified differential behavior by temporarily restoring the original fault (setProjectTrusted(true)): the script failed with AssertionError 'bootstrap pass leaked project extensions into trust resolution: ["cli.ts","project.ts","user.ts"]' at the core invariant assertion, then passed again after restoring the fix. Extension arrays are normalized with Array.from because the loaded module lives in a separate VM realm; without that, prototype-sensitive deep equality misfires. Limitation: the repository has no installed node_modules, so vitest (packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts) could not be executed and no dependencies were installed; the standalone VM-based regression was the focused validation instead.
